text:
maria: FYI we have a customer reporting a burst of 5xxs on hosted inference around 09:15 UTC. Errors all show control-plane 502/503, and some 500s that trace back to config DB timeouts + routing-policy service returning 500.

samir: thanks — can you paste the request-id and a sample gateway log? also which tenant?

maria: tenant=acme-inc, request-id=req_8f3a2cd. Sample gateway trace: 
```
[09:15:22.345] gateway -> controlplane: POST /v1/generate tenant=acme-inc id=req_8f3a2cd
[09:15:22.350] controlplane error: routing-policy service timeout (500) while evaluating policy for tenant=acme-inc
[09:15:22.351] controlplane -> gateway: 502 Bad Gateway (upstream timeout: configdb kv-read)
```
There are also auth/session handshakes failing intermittently with 504s.

infra-bot: alert: controlplane-configdb-latency spike detected (09:14-09:18 UTC) — 95th p90 latency >> baseline. Auto-retries suppressed by client. :warning:

olivia: Is this correlating with any deploy or config push? I don't see any canary or rollout in last 2 hours.

maria: no deploys. Metrics show a sudden jump in configdb read latency and connection saturation on the routing-policy pool.

leo: quick mitigation idea — can support route the customer to fallback routing policy (cached default) and bypass realtime policy evaluation? might reduce pressure. Also consider increasing configdb read pool / short-term cache TTL to warm KV.

support-oncall: I've told the customer we're investigating and recommended a retry/backoff (exponential, jitter) as a short-term client-side mitigation. They've seen ~30% failure rate on their traffic, high impact.

samir: repro steps for eng: run a tight loop against hosted API with X-Tenant: acme-inc and X-Request-ID header, and simulate ~200 concurrent requests to reproduce latency spike. Example:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: acme-inc" -H "X-Request-ID: test-$i" \
    -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate &\ndone; wait
```
This should surface routing-policy timeouts and configdb kv-read errors in controlplane logs.

olivia: I'll open a P0 on configdb pool and routing-policy service. Action items:
- increase configdb connection pool by +50% temporarily
- add short (5s) in-memory cache for routing-policy results for tenant acme-inc
- enable additional logging for KV read latency

maria: noted — also recommending a short-term control-plane fallback: if routing-policy returns 5xx, fall back to cached default policy and return 200 with warning header `X-Policy-Fallback: true`. That should keep customer traffic flowing.

samir: assigning to eng-infra & eng-runtime. I'll take primary on the rollback/mitigation. logging ticket: INF-4521.

support-oncall: customer update queued. Will escalate to AE if SLA window breached.

maria: I'll push the sample logs and request-ids to the incident doc and follow up once pool increase and fallback are live. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
